Source step. `open_buffer()` consumes the remaining fuzzer payload and constructs the datastream object later shared across all parser layers. On the witnessed run the constructor stores `buf = buffer`, `streampos = 0`, and `streamsize = 71` for the exact 71-byte payload named by ASan.

The staged payload begins with `II`, so `parse_tiff()` accepts little-endian order and reads the first IFD offset `doff = 8`. It then seeks to byte 8 and invokes `parse_tiff_ifd(base)` on that attacker-chosen IFD location.

The first IFD entry decoded at byte 8 has `tag = 0x8606` and `len = 2`, so its value stays inline in the 4-byte IFD slot. `parse_tiff_ifd()` therefore dispatches `parse_mos(ftell(ifp))` with the current cursor at byte 18, the start of inline bytes `STKP`.

Starting from offset 18, `parse_mos()` accepts the `STKP` marker, skips four space bytes, reads the 40-byte key string `ShootObj_back_type\0                         `, then consumes four more space bytes as `skip = 0x20202020`. After those reads `from = ftell(ifp) = 70`, so only one in-bounds payload byte remains.

The key string from step 4 matches `ShootObj_back_type`, so `parse_mos()` takes this branch and calls `fscanf(ifp, "%d", &i)` with the stream positioned at byte 70. At that point the only remaining in-bounds byte is ASCII `2` and there is no later in-bounds delimiter byte.

`fscanf` from step 5 expands to `scanf_one`, which calls `sscanf()` on `buf + streampos`. Here `streampos == 70`, so the format `%d` parses the last in-bounds byte `'2'`, stores `i = 2`, and returns `scanf_res = 1` while leaving `streampos` unchanged.

Root-cause step. Because step 6 returned `scanf_res > 0`, the delimiter-walk block executes. With `streampos == 70` and `streamsize == 71`, this loop condition still passes even though the scan started on the last byte and there is no in-bounds byte left to classify as a delimiter.
The first loop iteration advances `streampos` from the last valid index 70 to one-past-end index 71 and increments the delimiter-scan counter.

Sink step. With `streampos == 71`, the first `buf[streampos]` probe dereferences `buf[71]`, exactly one byte past the 71-byte region. The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this line and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of that region.

anchors.note: Source. `open_buffer()` is the first project statement that materializes the attacker-controlled remaining payload as a LibRaw datastream object.
Root cause. The post-scan delimiter walk treats the last valid byte position as safe loop entry, so it can increment `streampos` to one-past-end before any bounds check on `buf[streampos]`.
AddressSanitizer crash site. After the loop increments `streampos` past the last valid byte, the first delimiter probe dereferences one byte beyond the 71-byte heap buffer.
